BREAKING: SpaceXSI cuts invoicing time from 24 hours to minutes with Grok Bot.

Five specialized Grok Bots are now handling entire accounting jobs at SpaceXSI, with people stepping in for decisions and approvals:

• Customer accounts: Checks signed contracts, sets up customer access and removes access after contracts end.

• Billing: Checks contract details, catches errors and sends invoices—reducing the process from roughly 24 hours to minutes.

• Billing support: Answers questions and updates billing records. SpaceXSI estimates this bot alone saves its accounting team around 8 hours of work a day.

• Payments: Matches incoming payments to invoices and investigates differences. Work that normally takes an accountant 3–4 hours now takes roughly 30 minutes.

• Customer inquiries: Answers customer billing questions and coordinates requests such as refunds, which still require human approval.

SpaceXSI estimates that handling this workload without Grok Bot would require more than doubling its accounting team. Its accountants can now focus on improving systems and resolving complex issues.

SpaceXSI is showing how powerful Grok Bot can be for businesses: faster work, less time spent on routine tasks and more time for people to focus on what needs their expertise.

A SpaceX competitor explains just how impossible it is to achieve what Elon has.

Rocket Lab CEO Peter Beck once said reusable rockets didn't make sense for small rockets like his Electron. He promised he'd eat his hat if he ever changed his mind.

In 2019, with SpaceX already landing rockets, he walked on stage and admitted he was wrong.

Then he explained why he'd doubted it. The rocket comes back at "eight and a half times the speed of sound," through plasma "about half the temperature of the sun," with loads like "three elephants" standing on "a 1.8 mm carbon fibre rocket."

"Getting through the wall is really, really hard."

SpaceX first landed an orbital-class rocket booster upright on December 21, 2015.

The first two features Matt Palmer walks through in his What's new in Grok Bot 1.0 video this morning, Team Bot improvements and bots that join your meetings, are the same two things I asked for right here on X. On August 30 I wrote that we need to be able to share Grok Bots across teams, and Elon replied "Coming soon." On October 25 I suggested the Grok Bot team let my bot join a Zoom or Teams call with me, or for me, and Elon replied "This might be possible." Meetings started switching on for users less than two weeks later, and now both features lead the 1.0 release.

That says a lot about how responsive this team is. A user describes a need, Elon weighs in himself, and within weeks it is in the product and getting better. Any bot can now become a Team Bot at the flip of a switch, you choose exactly who it is shared with, and a new analytics tab shows the hours it has saved. In a meeting, the bot listens, answers in the chat and picks up spoken instructions, pulling what you need from your connected tools while the meeting is still going. The tempo of Grok Bot's evolution is extraordinary. And these are only two of the many new features in 1.0, so watch Matt's video to see just how fast Grok Bot is improving. I'm grateful to Matt, the team and Elon for listening.

最近硅谷两大佬因为马斯克吵翻了，结果老马亲自下场，一句话把全网看乐了。

先是著名反垄断评论家 Matt 泼冷水：SpaceX 算什么奇迹？马斯克根本不是天才，无非是会找华尔街搞钱，用钞票和工程师硬堆出来的。

这话连平时谁都不服的硅谷传奇程序员 DHH 都看不下去了，直接回怼：太酸了！哪怕你不喜欢马斯克，也得承认他“把吹过的牛变成现实”的能力举世无双。从特斯拉、脑机接口到 SpaceX，世上有一百万个会搞钱的投资人，但只有一个马斯克。

随后马斯克本尊下场，只回了一句灵魂反问：“行，那你给我解释一下蓝色起源、波音和 ULA？”

这一刀，直接捅在了“唯金钱论”的肺管子上。

如果光靠砸钱就能上天，那现在的太空霸主绝不可能是 SpaceX：
1、 比谁更有钱？ 贝索斯的蓝色起源比 SpaceX 早成立两年，背后站着前世界首富，从来不缺钱，结果到现在还在努力追赶。

2、 比谁补贴多？ NASA 当年搞载人航天，同一个任务，给波音砸了 42 亿美元，给 SpaceX 只给了 26 亿。结果 SpaceX 从 2020 年就开始像公交车一样送宇航员上天，波音的飞船却连宇航员都接不回来，最后还得靠 SpaceX 去救场。

3、 比华尔街输血？ SpaceX 起步根本没有华尔街一分钱，全是马斯克卖掉 PayPal 后自己掏的 1 亿美元家底。猎鹰 1 号连炸三次后差点破产，第四次才绝处逢生。

DHH 说得太对了：钱能买来顶级工程师，但买不来“不怕炸火箭”的魄力。

看看星舰第 15 次试飞（Flight 15）就懂了：同一个任务里，助推器在海里丢了，但飞船却从轨道返航、被发射塔的“机械筷子”稳稳夹住。

放在传统航天巨头那里，“丢了助推器”这半句话，就够他们停飞开两年的事故批斗会了；但在 SpaceX，这只是通往成功的又一组实验数据。

@elonmusk 说实话，到底哪个更难造：是一枚能上天的火箭，还是一家“允许工程师靠炸火箭来试错”的公司？

posts.name: Elon Musk
posts.text:
A lot of people have real trouble thinking about the aggregate behavior of groups. They can only think about individuals.

So they think about Elon Musk as an individual. Maybe they think that he must be retarded, because they need that for emotional reasons. Or maybe they think he is a talented rocket designer.

But even if they realize he understands rockets, they can only think about him as an individual doing tasks. Not about his impact on what the whole company does.

If Elon Musk is just a talented rocket designer, then he can spend all day, every day, improving rocket designs.

But he is just one of 7000 engineers. So even if did a perfect job, he would only improve progress by about .014%

So, when a midwit looks at SpaceX, he sees 7000 engineers, and says to himself "Elon Musk cannot possibly be designing the whole damn rocket himself. These people are giving him too much credit."

This would be absolutely true if Musk were just a some random SpaceX engineer. But he isn't. He's the absolute dictator of the whole damn company.

He decides, with absolute and unquestionable authority, which behaviors are punished and which are rewarded.

Why is this important?

When I worked at Boeing, on various classified projects, I naively came in with the assumption that I was a software engineer, employed to design and build functional software as quickly and cheaply as possible.

Because of this, I focused on functionality and efficiency, for example suggesting changes that would obviate the need for entire projects and software components.

And I very rapidly became persona non grata.

At first, this caused me to adopt an air of aggrieved innocence. I was just trying to do my job well, and I was being punished for it.

Then I gradually came to realize that I hadn't properly understood what my job was, or what the actual mission of Boeing Defense, Space, and Security was.

Boeing DSS was not an aerospace company. Boeing DSS was a fraud company.

Its goal was twofold. First, to maximize transfer of public tax dollars to stockholder pockets. Second, to maintain the appearance of being an aerospace company, to prevent the fraud from being exposed.

Which meant that my real job was twofold. First, to generate billable hours. Second, to look busy.

This is why Space Launch System sucks. Why it is always late when it doesn't fail outright. Why it is at 300% of its target budget. Why it leaves American astronauts stranded and needing a lift from SpaceX.

That's because, for Boeing, building rockets is a side quest. Something they have to do to look busy. Yes, a rocket does occasionally fly, but that's just happening so programs don't get shut down.

For Boeing, coming in early and under budget would actually be failure. The system is functioning exactly as designed.

The cost, not the rocket, is the goal.

Musk and SpaceX don't work like that.

Unlike Boeing executives, Musk is not a useless grifter asshole. He is an entirely different kind of asshole... a rocket obsessed sperg.

So, at SpaceX, engineers do not get rewarded for generating billable hours. They get rewarded for making rockets fly. And for all the subtasks of this, like figuring out how to make rockets lighter, figuring out how to make engines reignite better, figuring out how to make rocket exhaust not destroy launch pads, etc.

And this attracts engineers who care about rockets. You've seen them on broadcasts, crying on open microphones because they dedicated their lives to something and it just flew.

As a rocket engineer, who designs rockets, Musk is probably replaceable. As a rocket company engineer, who designs rocket companies, he is not.

For over 50 years, the US space industry stagnated precisely for the lack of a Musk-like figure, who could not only create an effective aerospace company, but who could thereby demonstrate what an effective aerospace company looks like.

Which makes it much more difficult for fraudsters to get away with fraud.

I'm envious. I wish I could have worked for an aerospace company instead of a fraud company.

But what's more important is that some of us now no longer have to play "who gets the most cheese?".

They get to play "What can we build today?".

posts.name: Elon Musk
posts.text:
What was the significance of this weekend's SpaceX tower catch:

"Catching the second stage is substantially harder than catching the first stage because the Ship returns from orbit while the booster returns from a short suborbital hop. The booster separates minutes after liftoff, performs a brief boostback, and comes back from only a few hundred kilometers away at relatively low speed. Ship must reach orbital velocity, deploy payload, coast for many hours, execute a precise deorbit burn, survive full reentry heating, and only then perform its landing burn. As such, Ship must carry a functional heat shield, fly a long guided atmospheric trajectory from the other side of the planet, and execute a high-energy flip into the “chopsticks” while protecting its heat-shield side. Those combined demands of orbital energy, thermal protection, long-range guidance, and final precision are why a Ship catch is so incredibly difficult. No prior system, including the Space Shuttle, recovered a rocket-style orbital stage in this manner. The catch validates the path to full reusability which is the foundation of Starship’s cost and cadence targets. This is particularly important in driving the economics of orbital data centers." - DB

posts.text: We've all read about Elon's working style being different. Hands-on, to say the least. Here's my anecdotal Elon moment: in 2014, we were raising capital and got introduced to John Doerr through our friend Jerry Murdock, and John wanted to meet me and Nami in Sicily, where they had a private event. During the evening, we jumped on a small bus together with Elon to join a dinner. At that time, Tesla had just opened their first showroom in Sweden, Täby. I told Elon that I booked a test ride with their new Model S but was wondering why they had a two-month waiting time to try the car. He was shocked/frustrated about the waiting time. He picked up his phone, made a call and sent some messages. The next week, Tesla Sweden called me and said, "Hi, you signed up for the test drive. We just got many more demo cars delivered and you can come and try it today already." That's how you get shit done! Can't even imagine how he operates today, but I'm sure it's still in the details and solving problems. That was inspiring, to say the least.

posts.text:
Morgan Stanley’s Adam Jonas on @SpaceX successfully catching Starship on flight 15:

“In our view, Flight 15 is a historic inflection moment for the company and spaceflight as a whole. SpaceX has recovered three Starship + many hundreds of Falcon 9 boosters in its history, and now others have accomplished the same. However, no entity has ever even attempted to recover a rocket upper stage in history (not counting Space Shuttle) given the intense thermal and mechanical stress of orbital re-entry.

With an upper stage now recovered intact, SpaceX can conduct a deep inspection of Ship 42 and use the findings to improve future vehicles in a way that was never previously possible. We believe it also helps clear the path to ramping full reuse of both booster and ship, the last major technical milestone before weekly or even daily Starship flights become realistic.

With a ship catch, SpaceX has materially de-risked the longer-term TAMs across all 3 of its segments.”

ref.text:
Elon Musk reveals he recruited SpaceX’s first engineers by telling them 'we’re probably going to die', and ended up as chief engineer because no good one would join

“So SpaceX, I started that in mid-2002 expecting to fail. Probably 90% chance of failing.”

“And even when recruiting people, I didn’t try to make out that it would work. I said, we’re probably going to die, but there’s a small chance we might not die, and this is the only way to get people to Mars and advance the state of the art.”

“And then I ended up being chief engineer of the rocket, not because I wanted to, but because I couldn’t hire anyone who was good. None of the good chief engineers would join, because they’re like, this is too risky, you’re going to die. And so I ended up being chief engineer of the rocket.”

posts.text:
Yes, the green flame is caused by burning copper from depleting fuel in the regenerative cooling circuit and going oxygen-rich (closer to stoichiometric temperature) in the main combustion chamber.

Slight underperformance of engines on this flight is the reason. The booster is meant to land with tiny residuals, so the solution is to improve engine performance and performance consistency (underway with Raptor V3.2), as well as adjust flight software to do MECO1 about one second earlier to ensure enough propellant for boostback and landing (tiny change).

These early ships and boosters are already outdated by improved designs in production or on the test stand, so this booster loss does not change our timeline to reach high volume, fully reusable Starship flights.

• Massive expansion: SemiAnalysis projects the Memphis–Mississippi campus will grow from 0.4 GW of IT capacity in January to 2.4 GW by the end of 2026. That would be a sixfold increase in one year.

posts.name: Elon Musk
posts.text:
SemiAnalysis’s Dylan Patel says Google’s TPUs are just as good as Nvidia’s in his nightly benchmarks, and without Jensen’s wheeling and dealing Google could take a ton of share

“It’s sort of a three-pronged strategy. One is you have to have the technical progress, and that keeps you winning. The second is that you have to have supply chain prowess, and Jensen’s the only executive in the semiconductor industry that is going out there and drinking and meeting and convincing all of these supply chain companies to invest like they’ve never done before, give him the allocations.”

“Now if all of a sudden there’s no Jensen, and Google’s like, actually, double my allocation. The TPU, from our benchmarking, we test TPUs. We run benchmarks on them on open source models every night. They’re just as good as Nvidia. But Google doesn’t have that DNA of wheeling and dealing with the supply chain, wheeling and dealing with customers. Now if that DNA is gone, the thing that is Jensen is gone, does that now mean Google can just take a ton of share? It’s a real big possibility.”

“Same with AMD. Technically, they’re awesome, but they’re just not able to wheel and deal like Jensen is able to. And that’s been a lot of the reason why they’ve been behind. Of course, the software as well. One of Nvidia’s biggest moats being CUDA, and software is being rapidly displaced by the fact that AI models are so good at writing software.”

These guys are fucking good. AMD. They’re all really good, and all these startups.”

“They’re all good. It’s not like they’re incompetent. I think it’s very different. As great as Lisa Su is, she took down Intel, who’s incompetent.”

posts.name: Elon Musk
posts.text:
Zambia has started connecting 751 health facilities across all 10 provinces with Starlink, and the first 90 kits went to Western Province.

There's something poetic about where they started. Every year at the end of the rainy season the upper Zambezi floods the Barotse plain, and for centuries the Lozi king has left his compound at Lealui by royal barge and moved to higher ground at Limulunga. The ceremony is called Kuomboka. In Lozi it means "to get out of water."

Now picture running fiber or building towers across land that turns into a lake for part of every year. A Starlink dish only needs a clear view of the sky, so the water below stops being the problem.

In March 2020, months before Starlink had its first beta users, Elon Musk said it would serve the 3 or 4 percent hardest-to-reach customers, people with no connectivity or really bad connectivity. Six years later, with funding from the Global Fund through Zambia's Ministry of Health, clinics on one of Africa's great floodplains are being brought into the country's electronic health systems from orbit.

posts.name: Elon Musk
posts.text:
Je viens de regarder mon passage dans Quotidien. Évidemment, je suis qualifié d’« influenceur entrepreneur d’extrême droite ».

Déroulons.

Je ne sais pas si vous vous rendez compte à quel point le peuple français vous méprise.

Vous êtes tellement déconnectés du réel que, dans votre petit monde, vous êtes persuadés d’avoir le monopole du bon sens. Alors je vais vous dire ce que vous êtes vraiment. Mais avant, je vais vous dire d’où je parle.

Je suis breton. J’ai grandi dans un système scolaire profondément cassé. La majorité de mes profs étaient de gauche, et la plupart étaient déprimés. Pas méchants. Déprimés. Ils ne transmettaient qu’une chose : la conviction que le monde est injuste, que l’effort ne paie pas, et que demain sera pire qu’hier.

Ce qui m’a sauvé, c’est d’avoir appris seul. J’ai commencé à coder à 12 ans. À 15 ans, j’avais créé un jeu qui me rapportait plus que le salaire de mes profs. Personne ne m’a donné la permission. Personne ne m’a subventionné. J’ai construit, des gens ont joué, j’ai été payé. La leçon d’économie la plus honnête de ma vie.

Ensuite j’ai travaillé dans la tech, j’ai vécu dans la Silicon Valley, j’ai construit pas mal de choses. Et j’ai étudié l’économie par moi-même. Pas pour un diplôme. Pour comprendre comment le monde fonctionne vraiment.

Et surtout, j’ai eu une chance que vous n’aurez jamais. J’ai été connecté, et je le suis encore, aux deux extrémités de la société. D’un côté, les couches les plus modestes, celles que vous prétendez protéger et incarner sans jamais leur parler. De l’autre, les couches les plus hautes : des milliardaires, des bâtisseurs, Elon Musk. Je fais le grand écart tous les jours. Et je peux vous dire une chose : en bas comme en haut, le diagnostic est le même. Vous, vous êtes au milieu, dans le seul étage de l’immeuble qui n’a pas de fenêtre.

Ce que je vais dire maintenant, n’importe quelle personne saine d’esprit qui a un contact avec le réel le comprend.

Yann, tu incarnes un mouvement et des idées qui ne représentent quasiment plus que vous. Ceux qui croient encore Quotidien et ses mensonges répétés en boucle, ce sont deux populations. Les gamins endoctrinés par une école capturée par l’idéologie. Et une partie des Français issus de l’immigration, qu’on manipule en leur répétant que les Français sont racistes. Un récit construit de toutes pièces par cette gauche mortifère, qui a besoin de victimes pour exister et qui les enferme dans ce rôle pour garder leurs voix.

Les idées que vous défendez sont des idées de mort. Elles culpabilisent le travail. Elles humilient ceux qui construisent. Elles transforment chaque citoyen en assisté ou en suspect. Partout où elles ont été appliquées jusqu’au bout, elles ont produit la même chose : la pauvreté, la défiance, l’effondrement. Pas une exception. Pas une.

Je le dis souvent : dans votre camp, il y a les cyniques et les believers. Les cyniques savent que ça ne marche pas, mais ça leur rapporte de l’audience, du pouvoir, des subventions. Les believers, eux, y croient sincèrement.

Yann, je vais te laisser le bénéfice du doute. Je te range dans la case des believers. Alors un conseil : lis Hayek. La Route de la servitude. Ça se lit en un week-end, et ça t’expliquera pourquoi chaque bonne intention que tu défends à l’antenne pave exactement la route que tu prétends combattre.

Tu as sans doute l’impression d’être du bon côté de l’histoire. Ils l’avaient tous. Mais tout ce que tu représentes enverra la France dans le chaos total.

Les gens que tu appelles « extrême droite », ce sont des gens normaux. Des gens qui veulent vivre en sécurité, travailler, être payés dignement pour ce qu’ils font, et élever leur famille dans un pays qu’ils reconnaissent encore. C’est tout. Ce n’est pas une idéologie. C’est le bon sens que vous avez abandonné, puis insulté.

Et je ne sais pas si vous mesurez ce qui est en train de se passer. Les peuples, dans leur intégralité, et avec eux les entrepreneurs, les créateurs de valeur, tous ceux qui font tourner ce pays, commencent à vous détester. Pas à vous critiquer. À vous détester, profondément, viscéralement. Chaque leçon de morale, chaque étiquette, chaque sketch condescendant creuse un peu plus le fossé. Alors un conseil d’ami : calmez-vous. Vraiment.

Je viens d’un milieu très loin des salons feutrés parisiens et des dîners bobos où l’on décide entre soi qui a le droit de parler. Toi, tu vis dans une bulle. Une bulle confortable, chauffée, avec un public qui rit au signal.

Mais le réel ne rit pas au signal.

Plus personne ne vous croit. Et le réel vous jugera. Très sévèrement.

What's happening at Starbase, Texas is truly incredible.

Deep in south Texas, Musk and his team have pulled in some of the most brilliant people on Earth to make space travel as normal and boring as air travel.

The energy there is just insane. It feels like a modern day Manhattan project, but built for peace not war.

The building pictured below is the actual factory where they build Starship, like a car factory for spaceships. You probably wouldn't have guessed it, since it looks like a nice office building. Most factories are cold and industrial but Starfactory feels warm, clean, with design touches that make you feel like you're in Silicon Valley.

There's something really special happening here. I envy everyone who gets to work here and live here. Most people never get a chance to devote themselves to something so meaningful, something that potentially bends the river of human history. It kind of feels like a college town, except everyone's building spaceships instead of going to class.

posts.text:
Guten Morgen zusammen,
heute vor elf Jahren, am 13. November 2015, verübten mehrere Attentäter im Namen des Islams, organisierte Anschläge in Paris. Der Horror dauerte über 4 Stunden und forderte 130 Todesopfer sowie knapp 700 Verletzte.

Zuerst sprengte sich gegen 21.17 Uhr ein Selbstmordattentäter in der Nähe des Stadion Stade de France in die Luft und riss dabei einen Menschen mit in den Tod. Der Attentäter wollte eigentlich ins Stadion gelangen. Hier fand gerade ein Freundschaftsspiel zwischen der Deutschen und Französischen Fußballnationalmannschaft vor 80.000 Zuschauern statt. Sein Sprengstoffgürtel wurde jedoch von einem Sicherheitsmann entdeckt, worauf der Attentäter flüchtete. Ein weiterer Sprengstoffattentäter versuchte fast zeitglich ins Stadion zu gelangen, scheiterte ebenfalls und sprengte sich am Toreingang H in die Luft, zum Glück ohne weitere unschuldige Menschen mitzureißen. Beide Attentäter trugen einen gefälschten syrischen Pass mit sich, und beide sollen im Oktober als Flüchtlinge in Griechenland registriert worden sein. Da die Pässe gefälscht waren, ist die Identität der Beiden bis heute nicht bekannt.

Beinah zeitgleich fuhr ein sogenanntes Hit-Team in einem Seat Leon vor eine Bar in einem Pariser Stadtteil. Sie feuerten dort mit Kalaschnikows auf die Gäste, die im Außenbereich saßen. Anschließend schossen sie auf Gäste eines gegenüberliegenden Restaurants. Insgesamt 15 Menschen verloren ihr Leben dort. Nach diesem Anschlag fuhren die Attentäter weiter, erschossen in einem Auto einen Mann und in einem Café, einem Waschsalon und in einem Restaurant noch vier Menschen. Anschließend begaben sich die Attentäter zur Bar "La Belle Équipe". Sie erschossen dort weitere 19 Menschen. 15 Menschen wurden teils schwer verletzt. Ein Selbstmordattentäter sprengte sich in einem Café in die Luft. Die Bombe detonierte unvollständig, weswegen hier keine weiteren Todesopfer zu beklagen waren, 15 Menschen wurden jedoch teils schwer verletzt.

Rund eine halbe Stunde nach dem ersten Attentat am Stadion begann der Horror im Bataclan Theater, wo gerade die US-Band Eagles of Death Metal ein Konzert vor rund 1.500 Zuschauern gab. Zwei Attentäter erschossen zuerst zwei Radfahrer vor dem Theater.
Anschließend drangen sie in das Gebäude ein und schossen mit Kalaschnikows -Gewehren zehn Minuten lang auf die Konzertbesucher. Zusätzlich warfen sie Handgranaten in die Menschenmenge. Einen Angreifer konnten zwei Polizisten töten, mussten sich aber dann wieder zurückziehen und auf Verstärkung warten. Zwei weitere Attentäter nahmen Geiseln und verschanzten sich im Gebäude. Um 0:50 Uhr erfolgte der Zugriff durch die Polizei. Die beiden Attentäter sprengten sich dabei in die Luft. 3 Stunden dauerte das Massaker im Bataclan Theater. 89 Menschen verloren dabei ihr Leben.

Der IS bekannte sich später zu den Anschlägen. Einige der Attentäter kamen als Flüchtlinge getarnt nach Europa. Der mutmaßliche Bombenbauer war zusammen mit zwei weiteren Attentätern kurze Zeit in Ulm. Sie stiegen dort in einem Hotel in der Stadt ab, und wurden dort von einem weiteren Attentäter abgeholt.

Zeugenaussagen von Menschen, die diese Hölle überlebt haben:

„Wir dachten zuerst, es seien Knallkörper. Dann sah es hinten im Saal nach Funken aus. Rasch wurde klar, dass es sich um Mündungsfeuer handelte. Drei Männer mit Gewehren schossen den Zuschauern in den Rücken und stürmten weiter, in die Menge schießend.“

„Das Trio war unvermummt, mit kurzen Bärten. Einer befahl den über tausend Zuschauern, sich auf den Boden zu legen. In akzentfreiem Französisch erklärte er: Ihr habt in Syrien unsere Brüder getötet, jetzt sind wir hier.“

„Sie sagten, wenn ihr euch bewegt, töten wir euch. Sie erschossen die auf dem Boden liegenden Leute trotzdem.“
„Sie töteten, töteten, töteten. Ich war von Toten umgeben. Ich weiß nicht, wie ich überlebt habe.“

„Sie waren schwarz gekleidet. Einer hatte ein sehr jungenhaftes Gesicht, und er ging seelenruhig zur Sache. Er ging sehr methodisch zu Werke, töteten eiskalt einen nach dem anderen.“

„Sein Blut ergoss sich auf mein Bein. Meinen Nachbarn, einen Mann von 50 Jahren, traf ein Schuss direkt ins Gesicht; Stücke seines Hirn fielen auf meine Brille. Ich hörte die Kugeln und versuchte, auf den Boden zu schauen. Da war eine riesige Blutlache.“

„Merkwürdigerweise hört man die Kugeln fast nicht, wenn sie von der Nähe aus abgeschossen werden. Aber ich spürte ihre Hitze an der Wange. Ich war bereit zu sterben. Ich wog damals 122 Kilo, 20 mehr als heute. Wenn einer getroffen wird, dann ja wohl ich.“

„Irgendjemand schaltete das Licht in der Halle an. Keine Ahnung, wer das war. Ich erkannte den Mann, der gerade noch neben mir an der Bar etwas geholt hatte. Er lag am Boden, sein halbes Gesicht war zerstört. Er war tot.“

„Ich lag auf dem Bauch. Meine Freunde waren neben mir. Wir haben langsam und leise geredet. Die Freunde hatten Kinder, ich nicht. Sie hatten mehr Angst als ich. Der rechts sagte: Ich muss meine beiden Kinder wiedersehen.“

„Wenn ein Meteorit irgendwo einschlägt, sind alle sofort tot. Die eigentliche Folter war, dass sie die Leute einzeln erschossen haben. Manche schrien noch Gnade. Schon wurden sie erschossen.“

„Einmal schrie ein Attentäter: Wenn einer nach Hause will, dann jetzt“ Einzelne sind aufgestanden, die wurden gleich erschossen. Auf dem Boden war Blut. Überall waren Tote und Blut.“

„Ich stieg über einen Mann am Boden. Ich nahm seine Hand, doch sie war schlaff und kühl. Ein paar Meter weiter sah ich eine junge Frau, sie war am Rücken getroffen worden. Leute sind auf sie gestiegen. Reflexhaft kauerte ich mich zu ihr, unter uns war eine Pfütze aus Blut.“

„Ich rannte zum großen Boulevard Voltaire, stolperte, verlor meine Brille. Ich drehte mich zurück zu dem Mann, über den ich gestolpert war und wollte mich entschuldigen. Beim Runterbeugen sah ich. Er war tot. Wir sind in ein Wohnhaus geflüchtet und klopften an Türen, aber niemand machte auf. Die Leute hatten Angst.“

„Nach gefühlt einer halben Stunde schrie jemand: Nicht bewegen, sonst schieße ich“

„Dann gab es eine Explosion. Mein linkes Ohr wurde taub davon. Es regnete Blut und menschliche Überreste auf uns.“

„Nach einer Weile kam ein Polizist vom Sondereinsatzkommando zu uns hoch und hielt eine kleine Ansprache, die ich nie vergessen werde. Er sagte: Ich freue mich, Sie alle zu sehen, denn Sie sind Überlebende des Bataclan. Sie sind Helden. Vergessen Sie das nie!“

posts.name: Elon Musk
posts.text:
In 2014, Elon Musk stood in front of an audience at MIT and told the whole world exactly where AI was going.

Everyone missed it. Because he used one word, and that's the only thing the internet remembered: "demon."

The headlines called him scared of killer robots. Tech blogs called it hyperbole. People moved on.

I went back and watched that moment. It's barely 2 minutes long. You'll never hear the word "AI" the same way again.

Here's what I took away.

1. He called it before almost anyone.

Someone in the audience asks about AI. His face goes serious.

"If I were to guess like what our biggest existential threat is, it's probably that. So we need to be very careful with the artificial intelligence."

This was 2014. No ChatGPT. Most people had never heard the word "chatbot."

2. He asked for rules 12 years ago.

"I'm increasingly inclined to think that there should be some regulatory oversight, maybe at the national and international level, just to make sure that we don't do something very foolish."

National AND international. In 2014.

Governments are still arguing about it today.

3. The demon line wasn't a joke.

"With artificial intelligence we are summoning the demon."

And then the part almost nobody quotes:

"In all those stories where there's the guy with the pentagram and the holy water, it's like, yeah, he's sure he can control the demon. Doesn't work out."

Read that again.

His warning wasn't about the demon. It was about the guy who thinks he can control it.

4. Now here's what got me.

In 2014 he said: summoning the demon.

In 2018 he told Joe Rogan: "Nobody listened."

In 2023 he signed a letter asking AI labs to pause.

In 2026 he told The Economist he can't see any way to stop it anymore. His new philosophy? "Let's enjoy the ride." And: "If you can't beat them, join them."

Today he's building one of the most powerful AIs on Earth.

12 years later, the man who warned us about the guy with the pentagram is holding one.

My takeaway:

He wasn't wrong in 2014. He just realized nobody was going to stop it. So he decided to build it himself.

Whether that's genius or the exact ending of his own story, I honestly don't know.

So now I'm asking you:

Was Musk right in 2014?

Or did he become the guy in his own warning?

Tell me below. I genuinely want to know where people land on this.

These are the community benefits if @SpaceX builds their planned $50 billion Arizona Supercomputing Campus:

• 6,500 jobs (1,000 permanent, 5,500 construction).
• Up to $103M annually in new property tax revenue.
• 10-40% lower electricity bills projected for local SSVEC residential customers.
• Up to $250M in one-time county sales tax revenue.
• Up to $460M annually in additional benefits for Arizona electric cooperative members.
• $3.6B in grid upgrades funded by SpaceX at no cost to cooperative members.
• 24 GWh of battery storage to improve grid stability and reliability.
• Additional solar energy to reduce strain on the local grid.
• Minimal water usage, with no new wells and zero ongoing industrial water consumption projected.
• Aquifer and wildlife protection, including conservation initiatives.
• Reduced noise and light pollution through noise mitigation and dark-sky protections.
• Support for local schools, infrastructure, businesses, and essential services.

quote.name: Sawyer Merritt
quote.text:
SpaceX has just unveiled a massive new $50 billion Supercomputing Campus that they want to build in Cochise County, Arizona.

All info:
• Up to 6 GW across the 9 supercomputing buildings
• Construction starts 2027
• Size of each supercomputing building: ~493,000 square feet.
• Total supercomputing building space: 4.44 million square feet, excluding support facilities.
• SSVEC residential customers are projected to see electricity bill reductions of 10–40%.
• Up to 24 GWh of grid-connected battery storage to provide backup power, stabilize the regional electric grid, support local voltage, and absorb fluctuations in electricity demand. Among the largest planned battery installations in the United States.
• Additional solar generation in the region is planned to supply renewable electricity during the day and reduce demand on the local grid.
• No dedicated on-site power plant or fuel storage yard is planned.
• Each supercomputing building will have 10 MW of natural-gas-powered standby generation for critical equipment, operating only during utility outages and periodic testing.
• No gas turbines will be installed at the site.
• SpaceX plans to fund $3.6 billion in grid infrastructure upgrades, transferred to AEPCO at no cost to its members.
• Up to $260 million annually in additional benefits for cooperative members at full buildout, on top of residential bill reductions.
• Up to $200 million annually for cooperative members statewide, in addition to SSVEC benefits.
• The supercomputers will use dry cooling with a closed-loop water circulation system rather than evaporative cooling.
• SpaceX projects zero ongoing industrial water consumption.
• The cooling system will be filled initially, with water reused for up to 10 years.
• SpaceX estimates annual water usage equivalent to approximately 20–30 Arizona residential homes.
• Projected annual water use would be less than 2.5% of a single center-pivot irrigation system's annual consumption.
• Permanent jobs: Approximately 1,000.
• Construction jobs: Approximately 5,500.
• Annual property tax revenue: Up to $103 million in estimated new annual revenue.
• Regional economic benefits: SpaceX says its investment will support public education, infrastructure, essential local services, and economic development.
• Local suppliers: SpaceX is encouraging suppliers to participate in construction and development of the campus.
• Noise mitigation: Equipment will be positioned away from neighboring properties where possible, with setbacks and additional screening to reduce noise.
• Nighttime lighting: Outdoor lighting will remain off unless work is underway, with active lights shielded and directed downward.
• Dark-sky protection: The campus will comply with Cochise County's dark-sky requirements to limit light pollution.
• Nighttime construction: SpaceX says it will seek waivers when nighttime construction lighting is necessary.
• Wildlife protection: The campus is being designed with consideration for the region's sandhill crane wintering habitat.

This campus's purpose is to build one of the world's most advanced AI supercomputing campuses to train SpaceX's superintelligence models and support scientific and engineering breakthroughs.

Learn more: https://www.spacex.com/sites/cochise-county

Why Elon Musk believes we could colonize the entire galaxy in a million years

To Elon Musk, it's not even a hard question.

A million years is enough to spread across the whole galaxy.

So where is everyone?

Nobody seems to have done it.

Something stops civilizations before they get out there. That's the great filter.

And it's why he thinks about Mars with one specific test.

Elon: "Do we have enough resources on Mars such that if the spaceships from Earth stopped coming, you can survive?"

Joe Rogan compared it to a long sea voyage where the only thing you're missing is vitamin C.

And the ships could stop for reasons that aren't dramatic at all.

Civilization on Earth could end with a bang or a whimper.

A Mars that can survive on its own is how he thinks we get past the filter.

posts.name: Elon Musk
posts.text:
Bot 1.0 is out. Our goal for this release was to make Bots a much more useful part of your team.

Some new things we're excited about:

- Bots can now join Zoom, Google Meet, and more. You can ask Bot questions in meetings and even assign it action items. We have ours taking standup notes every day in our shared Google Doc and doing background research on discussion themes. Soon, you'll be able to talk back and forth with it live in a meeting.

- A new interface for managing your Bots. You can see and steer their responsibilities, what they're learning, and their impact. It's impossible to build trust in an AI teammate if it's a black box, so it should proactively flag when it's blocked or confused, take and learn from feedback across the company, and be able to succinctly summarize its contributions.

- Better collaboration in Slack and Teams. Bots are more ambiently aware, carry context across conversations, and learn from your team over time. In our Slack, we regularly see threads between members of our team and multiple Bots, handing off work, context, and decisions. Bots should intuit your company's customs and how work gets done, not just execute on the specific tasks they're given.

posts.text:
Elon Musk has a track record of calling hard problems early.

In a February 2026 interview, he warned: “Those who have lived in software land don’t realize they’re about to have a hard lesson in hardware.”

By late August, SpaceX confirmed it was bringing the casting of gas-turbine blades and vanes in-house — the single biggest bottleneck for new natural-gas power plants needed to feed AI data centers. Musk said the move could bring turbines online up to 18 months faster.

Today he put it even more bluntly: SpaceX has “a super cracked team that is outperforming the rest of the world by an order of magnitude in mass to orbit — and even we find it very difficult.”

Hardware doesn’t care about demos, funding rounds, or slide decks. The teams that actually build the hard stuff keep winning.

What a legend.

quote.name: Elon Musk
quote.text:
It’s not that supercomputer data centers are not in high demand, as they definitely are. However, getting money to build complex hardware systems with massive power, cooling & networking is not the same as doing it.

SpaceX has a super cracked team that is outperforming the rest of the world by an order of magnitude in mass to orbit and even we find it very difficult!

posts.text:
Elon Musk just revealed a massive update on Grok 4.8, and SpaceXSI has completely rebuilt its reinforcement learning and inference infrastructure from scratch

The engineering team has abandoned JAX and SGLang, rewriting the entire RL and inference stack in C/C++

Here’s where Grok 4.8 stands:

• Pre-training is complete
• Major cleanup of supervised fine-tuning data
• Reinforcement learning now underway
• Evaluation scores are starting to climb
• Soft rollout to Grok Bot users planned for later this week

And Elon also gave another imp update about Grok 4.8:

“Grok 4.8 will bear no resemblance to 4.7 (thankfully)”

He also explained why the development took longer than expected:

“It is not yet incredible, but, this time, the foundations are built right, so I expect it to evolve to be something special”

This is a fundamental engineering overhaul, not just another model upgrade

SpaceXSI has rewritten the underlying infrastructure to build a much stronger foundation for Grok’s future development.

And the first Grok Bot users are expected to get their hands on it this week

quote.name: Elon Musk
quote.text:
We have dumped JAX/SGLang and rewritten the entire RL and inference stack from scratch in C/C++, which took some extra time.

Training (aka pre-training) is done. Lot of cleanup was needed on the SFT data to get that mostly right. Now, 4.8 is in RL and the evals are starting to climb. We will do a soft rollout to Bot users later this week and see how it goes.

Grok 4.8 will bear no resemblance to 4.7 (thankfully). It is not yet incredible, but, this time, the foundations are built right, so I expect it to evolve to be something special.

posts.name: Elon Musk
posts.text: Turns out that the Starlink software, built for managing the movement of vast amounts of data through space and to the ground, is also very well suited to training super intelligence

posts.name: Elon Musk
posts.text:
Elon Musk just revealed something huge about Grok's new SI training and inference infrastructure

The engineering behind Starlink is now helping power the development of Grok

SpaceXSI has completely rewritten Grok's reinforcement learning and inference software from scratch, replacing JAX and SGLang with its own system built primarily in C, with a little C++

And the most important part is where this engineering expertise comes from

The new stack is built on the incredible work of the engineers who created Starlink's incredibly complex satellite network

Elon explained:

"At SpaceX, we write our own headers and calculate our own time (includes leap seconds). Not many people will know what this means, but those that do will appreciate it."

Here's why that's significant

SpaceX engineers build and control critical parts of their software themselves, even down to the code interfaces and precise time calculations needed for satellite operations

This gives them much tighter control over how their systems operate, reducing unnecessary software dependencies and allowing them to optimize performance and reliability

Now that same engineering philosophy is being applied to Grok

posts.name: Elon Musk
posts.text:
In February 2004 Elon Musk wrote the check that put Tesla Motors on the road: $6.5 million of a $7.5 million Series A, plus the chairman's seat.

He led the next round in February 2005. He co-led the $40 million round in May 2006 that brought in Larry Page and Sergey Brin. That August he published The Secret Tesla Motors Master Plan on the company blog, a sports car to pay for an affordable car, and so on down to the mass market. He pushed for the Roadster's carbon fiber body. By January 2009, Bloomberg reported, he had put $70 million of his own money into the company.

CNBC still wrote this on September 10, 2018: "Though Musk didn't found Tesla, his DNA is very much a part of the company."

Read the very next sentence of the same article: "He was one of its original investors and chairman of the board in 2004 before becoming CEO in 2008."

Original investor. Chairman in 2004. CNBC typed both facts and still filed him under "didn't found."

That question had been settled nine years earlier, in court and in writing. In 2009 Martin Eberhard sued, and one of the things he asked a San Mateo County judge for was a declaration that he and Marc Tarpenning were the only two founders. In July the judge struck that request. In September the case was settled and Tesla named five co-founders: Eberhard, Tarpenning, Elon Musk, JB Straubel and Ian Wright.

Eberhard's own statement that day: "As a co-founder of the company, Elon's contributions to Tesla have been extraordinary."

The man who went to court over the title called Elon Musk a co-founder in his own words. A business network still decided it knew better.

Elon Musk has told his side too. In April 2022 he wrote that the Tesla he walked into was "a shell corp" with "literally nothing but a biz plan to commercialize AC Propulsion's Tzero car, which was introduced to me by JB Straubel, *not* Eberhard." Then: "If filing a shell corp constitutes 'founding a company', then I'd be the only founder of PayPal, since I filed the original incorporation docs for http://X.com (later renamed PayPal), but that's not what founding means."

And the line that says the most: "I put in all I had, whereas Eberhard, who was worth over $10M at the time, refused to invest a penny to help Tesla."

So why slip a false founder line into a 2018 piece? Look at the headline it sat under: "Musk's defiant, rebel CEO persona is putting his company and its investors at risk, say management experts." The article argued Tesla needed "someone to help keep Musk in line." Shrink his role at the birth of the company and it gets much easier to argue he is replaceable at the top of it. quote.name: Fireside Alpha
quote.text:
SpaceX’s Arizona data center, per a county supervisor: “We could be reducing property taxes across the board in Cochise County, the entire county, by 20%”

Frank Antenori, whose district includes the site, brought up the county’s tax math during a live Q&A:

“Here’s just something to just chew on. Arizona has an expenditure limit requirement that is placed on counties. If we exceed that expenditure, we have to rebate back to the taxpayers a certain amount.”

“So, if we’re receiving revenue in from SpaceX, by law, we have to offset that to the taxpayers. We have the potential to reduce, based on the projected revenue they’re creating, as much as 20%.”

“Let me just say it again. We could be reducing property taxes across the board in Cochise County, the entire county, by 20% to offset for the revenue here, because we can’t spend all that money. So, we have to give that money back to the taxpayers. The law says we have to.”

“So, you could see a potential significant impact to local property taxes. What that is, I don’t know. We’re going to have to do the math on it. But the law, if we have this large increase in property tax revenue, we have to balance those rates. So that will reduce dramatically the property tax burden of every resident in the county.”

“The construction sales tax, which also is the TPT, the transaction privilege tax, the retail tax, and the jail excise tax. So that will be part of the construction tax. We could literally use that money to pay the jail off in 2 to 3 years, as opposed to the 13 to 20 years.”

A battery cost $600 per kilowatt-hour. The materials it’s made of, according to Elon Musk, cost about $80.

REPORTER: Where does that gap come from?

ELON MUSK: Most people reason by analogy. They say batteries will always be expensive because they’ve always been expensive. That’s pretty dumb.

REPORTER: Why?

ELON MUSK: If you applied that reasoning to anything new, you’d never get to the new thing. You can’t say, “Horses are great, we’re used to them, and there’s no gasoline to buy, so nobody will ever want a car.” And people did say that.

REPORTER: So how should you reason?

ELON MUSK: From first principles, not by analogy. Normally we do something because it’s like something that was done before, or because other people are doing it.

REPORTER: What are first principles?

ELON MUSK: The physics way of looking at the world. You boil things down to the most fundamental truths and reason up from there.

REPORTER: Why doesn’t everyone do that?

ELON MUSK: Because it takes a lot more mental energy.

REPORTER: Can you give an example?

ELON MUSK: Batteries. Historically it’s $600 per kilowatt-hour, and they say it won’t get much better. I ask something else: what is it made of?

REPORTER: And what is it made of?

ELON MUSK: Cobalt, nickel, aluminum, carbon, some polymers for separation, and a sealed can.

REPORTER: And what does that cost?

ELON MUSK: At London Metal Exchange prices it comes to something like $80 per kilowatt-hour.

REPORTER: So that’s almost eight times less. What do you do with that?

ELON MUSK: Come up with clever ways to combine those materials into the shape of a battery cell. And then batteries can be much cheaper than anyone realizes.

‼️Dave Chappelle Must Be Canceled After Saying He Feels Better Since Charlie Kirk Was Murdered😡

Dave Chappelle stood on stage at Madison Square Garden and told the audience“Ever since that guy Charlie Kirk got murdered, and I shouldn’t say this publicly but…. I feel better.”  - Dave Chappelle

Those words are not edgy. They are not comedy. They are a public declaration that the assassination of a man who was speaking on a college campus  and standing up for his freedom of speech made him feel better. Charlie Kirk was a husband and a father. He was shot while engaging with students. Celebrating that outcome, or even admitting it brings relief, crosses a line that no amount of past comedic success can erase.

Every remaining date on Dave Chappelle’s schedule should be canceled. Venues, promoters, and sponsors who continue to platform someone who openly states he feels better because a political figure was murdered are choosing to normalize political violence. The audience that still shows up is making the same choice. This is not about hurt feelings. It is about whether society will continue to reward people who treat the murder of their political opponents as a source of personal satisfaction.

FUCK Dave Chapprlle

Elon Musk explains one of the most terrifying existential threats humanity faces: a massive comet striking Earth and potentially wiping out civilization

“Earth does not currently have any ability to stop asteroids. Now with Starship, we then have some ability to stop an asteroid actually, technically, a comet would be the real danger

Because there are billions, if not more than billions, maybe trillions of objects that are in the outer solar system, with very long-period comets

An example that most people are probably aware of is Halley’s Comet. It’s slightly under once per century that Halley’s Comet comes by. Many comets have very long periods that we simply don’t know exist

And for example, the comet Shoemaker-Levy when that hit Jupiter, it made a hole in Jupiter the size of Earth. So if that did hit Earth, game over "Everything’s dead"

So there’s always some risk of such a thing occurring, and the probable lifespan of life is just much greater if we’re a multi-planet and ultimately multi-stellar civilization”

Russell Brand’s ex-girlfriend Samantha Pressdee has fiercely spoken out against the verdict.
 She stated the following:
 "A wife is without her husband. Three children are without their Dad. Yet everyone thinks the real victim in this is a drunk groupie who was cheating on her boyfriend. Someone who has anonymity for life and will probably get a financial payout.
 “If this drunk groupie thought he was a predator, why would she stand by and watch him sleep with 1000s more women? Didn't she care about those women?
 "It's not true that women in the comedy industry warned each other about Russell. No one warned me, and it could not have been more obvious that I was connected to him. Just because I am a woman doesn't mean I should 'believe all women'.
 "I would be more likely to believe women who report criminals to the POLICE. Not the media, decades later. I believe in the right to a fair trial. Convince me it was fair!"
 She also slammed Georgina Bailey who claimed to be Brand’s ex-lover and had urged him to “tell the truth.”
 "She was a groupie too,” Samantha revealed. “The kind of women throwing themselves at Brand back then often sold kiss-and-tell [stories] that were mostly made up.
 "Russell paid for Georgina to go to rehab. Ballie has made a career out of sleeping with him. She's not his ex-girlfriend. At the time, she was in a burlesque troupe called 'The Satanic Sluts'."
 At the moment, we are being led to believe that Russell Brand is guilty beyond reasonable doubt. There is no evidence - only the word of one woman and more words from people who don’t like him.
 Now we have other words from someone who knew him that say the opposite of what the establishment and media are saying.
 I also found Reform MP Sarah Pochin’s comments on TalkTV disgraceful. In the clip, she spoke about Brand as if he was 100% guilty, spoke in a rather venomous way about him saying she hoped he would go away for a long long time, and spoke about the accusers as if they are bastions of truth even though there is no way she could possibly know that.
 This is trial by media. Trial by hearsay. Trial by dislike of one person. But trial by truth? No. Russell Brand faces serious danger in prison and was forbidden from saying goodbye to his kids. No mercy is being shown to him. I see only venom and hate. Yet I have seen Brand speak repeatedly about his faith for years, urging millions of people to find their own. The entire thing feels off and rancid. The more this case goes on and the more that is revealed by people like his ex-girlfriend, the more it becomes clear that something very wrong has happened here and we are in the midst of watching something very evil taking place.

SpaceX has outlined five contingency landing options for Starship Flight 15 as it prepares for the ship’s first tower-catch attempt at Starbase

This visualization shows how the mission can change course if the vehicle or tower does not meet the conditions required for a safe return:

1. Indian Ocean — after ascent
If the orbital insertion burn is skipped, Starship remains on its suborbital trajectory and reenters over a predetermined area of the Indian Ocean

2. North of Hawaii — early in the mission
If the flight needs to end shortly after reaching orbit, Starship returns to a designated area of the Pacific north of Hawaii

3. Off Chile — mid-mission
A separate return opportunity allows Starship to land in the eastern Pacific, far off the coast of Chile

4. Gulf offshore — catch contingency
If the tower catch is called off before final approach, Starship has an offshore landing option in the Gulf instead of proceeding with the catch

5. North of Hawaii — late in the mission
If the planned deorbit burn is skipped, Starship completes another orbit before returning to the Pacific north of Hawaii

The objective is to bring Starship home. The flight plan builds in alternatives throughout the journey, with continuous vehicle-health checks determining when to proceed

An ambitious mission, backed by carefully planned options from ascent to final approach

posts.text:
SpaceX has just released a new blog about Starship's upcoming 15th flight planned for Nov 13 with more info about what to expect, the significance of this flight, and their approach to safety:

"Starship is preparing to take a major step towards full reusability: bringing the Starship upper stage back to the launch site for a catch by the tower at Starbase.

To return Starship to Starbase, the spacecraft must now fly a safe trajectory that will take it over inhabited areas in northern Mexico and southern Texas to reach its launch site for catch. Like previous flight testing and the first successful mission to orbit, Starship’s flight profile for this ambitious mission is being designed with opportunities to safely end the mission early if necessary and will follow strict criteria before committing to the final phases of flight.

OUR APPROACH TO A SAFE RETURN:
On Flight 15, Starship will initially launch to a passively safe suborbital trajectory. This is the same flight profile used on Starship’s first orbital mission and ensures that any issues encountered during ascent or shortly thereafter will result in Starship reentering over a cleared area of the Indian Ocean.

After this initial ascent, flight controllers will assess the health of Starship’s systems before giving a “go” or “no-go” for orbit. If “go”, Starship will then perform an orbital insertion burn with a single Raptor sea-level engine, increasing its speed and achieving orbit around Earth.

Once on orbit, Starship will deploy its payload of Starlink V3 satellites. Three of these satellites have been modified to acquire imagery of Starship’s heatshield. This method of analyzing Starship’s heatshield has been tested on previous flights and is one of several data sources to help inform Starship’s readiness to return to the launch site on Flight 15.

After deploying its payload, Starship will then coast in orbit for another ~21 hours until its orbit aligns with Starbase for a return. During this multi-hour orbital coast, flight controllers will continuously perform manual and automated checks of Starship systems which, similar to the first orbital flight, will be intentionally conservative. They include Raptor engine health, loss of power or communications, the health of the flight computers and navigation sensors, the structural integrity of the propellant tanks and feedlines, the ability to hold tank pressure, and Starship’s ability to control its attitude.

During this prolonged coast phase, flight control teams have several options to end the mission early and return Starship to precleared areas of the Pacific Ocean if needed. These locations include early- and late-mission splashdown options around Hawaii and a mid-mission splashdown opportunity several hundred kilometers off the coast of Chile. These precleared areas, which were also used during Flight 14, provide a safe place to land Starship if any conditions arise that may preclude the ability to perform a safe reentry.

WHAT SHIP CATCH WILL LOOK (AND SOUND) LIKE:
Flight controllers will only permit Starship to return to Starbase if the vehicle’s status meets our internally developed, and FAA-approved, conditions for a return to launch site and catch.

If these requirements are met, Starship will perform a deorbit burn with a single Raptor 3 engine. This deorbit burn will alter Starship’s path to place the vehicle on a course to reenter Earth’s atmosphere at a specific point over the Pacific Ocean, thousands of kilometers uprange from Starbase.

During reentry, Starship can alter its flight path by moving its four control flaps. This will permit Starship to maintain a safe and known trajectory while guiding itself with high precision control toward Starbase. This control will also allow Starship to carry out a series of small turns in its trajectory to intentionally fly over sparsely populated areas of northern Mexico and southern Texas.

As Starship approaches Starbase from the west, the vehicle will weave its way around the major cities in the Rio Grande Valley, passing to the north of South Padre Island and out over the Gulf of America as it makes its final turn south towards Starbase. This banking maneuver has been demonstrated several times on previous Starship flight tests.

During this phase, residents of Cameron County and those in the nearby area may hear one or more sonic booms as Starship approaches the launch site. A sonic boom is a brief, thunder-like noise a person on the ground hears when an aircraft or other vehicle in the area flies faster than the speed of sound. The sonic boom does not present a health risk and what people experience will depend on weather and other conditions.

As Starship arrives over Starbase, it will perform the final bellyflop maneuver down towards the tower at Pad 2. This bellyflop was proven during a series of high-altitude test hops and during numerous suborbital flight tests. Shortly before reaching the tower, Starship will ignite its three sea-level Raptor engines and flip itself vertical while stowing its flaps. After the flip is complete, Starship will down-select to two Raptor engines and maneuver between the tower's mechanical arms, before down-selecting to a single engine as it comes to a near hover. The arms will close rapidly to catch Starship on its two catch fittings just below the forward flaps. Once Starship registers contact with the tower arms, it will shut down its final Raptor engine.

During reentry, flight controllers will have several options to end the reentry early and safely by intentionally tumbling Starship to ensure that it breaks up in the atmosphere before reaching land. There is also a late-reentry option to send Starship into the Gulf of America if any of its systems or the tower itself encounter an issue after reentry that would preclude a safe catch at Starbase.

THE HOLY GRAIL OF ROCKETRY:
Recovering an entire orbital launch system has never been done, and Starship has always been designed change that. This full recovery is often referred to as the Holy Grail of rocketry as it enables full and rapid reuse of a rocket – opening the door to airplane-like cadence where a vehicle flies again rapidly.

Reaching this milestone with Starship will allow SpaceX to unlock the true capability of Starship and will enable future missions to establish a permanent human presence on the Moon, expand the worldwide Starlink network, launch our Starmind supercompute constellation, extend the light of consciousness to the stars, and make life multiplanetary."

天呐，海底光缆统治世界的时代要结束了，又要见证历史了🤯。。
马斯克首次公布 Starlink V4 的极端参数：性能直接跳涨一百倍，光速天然快了一点四倍且不用绕大陆架，上千万条激光链路正在把地球通信主干搬上深空。

绝大多数人至今依然以为，星链只是给偏远山区、游艇和飞机提供网络补丁的边缘工具。
直到马斯克刚刚在最新的投资人会议上摊开底牌，很多人才第一次看懂 SpaceX 真正的阳谋：把构筑人类现代文明的海底光缆网络，从大洋深处连根拔起，彻底搬到太空。
这里藏着一个极度反直觉的物理常识： 光在太空真空中的传播速度，比在玻璃光纤里整整快了 40%。
 更致命的是几何路径的差异。海底光缆必须顺着大陆架和海沟蜿蜒曲折地绕远路，而太空中的卫星激光链路，两点之间永远是沿着大圆航线在真空中直线对穿。这意味着在跨洋超长距离通信上，太空激光的延迟天然比地面光缆更低。
而阻碍这件事过去的唯一瓶颈，是带宽密度。
马斯克这次直接给出了技术迭代的量化终局： 从 V2 到即将落地的 V4 卫星，单星吞吐能力将直接迎来 100 倍的暴力跃升。 在更长期的宏大蓝图里，超过 10 万颗卫星组成的轨道阵列，每颗都将配备大约 100 个传输速率超 10 Tbps 的光学激光器，在地球外围织成一张百 Exabit 级别的无缝高速网状路由。
这已经不是在做卫星宽带了，这是在用火箭把全球互联网的核心骨干网整个重写一遍。
海底光缆容易被地质地震震断、被船锚挂伤，更深陷地缘博弈的物理封锁；而悬在头顶的真空激光网络，既没有折射损耗，也没有无法逾越的地理边界。
人类用了上百年时间，把铜线和光纤一根根沉入海底来连接彼此；而未来的文明动脉，注定要在没有阻力的星空里以光速奔流。

SpaceX has officially announced that it is currently targeting November 13th at 5:45 PM ET for Starship's 15th flight.

Flight info:
"This flight is planned to be the first to return both Starship and Super Heavy to the launch site for catch. If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket."

• Flight will last more than 22 hours, completing approximately 14 orbits around Earth.
• Starship will orbit at an altitude of approximately 275 km (171 miles).
• First attempt to recover both Super Heavy and Starship at the launch site during the same mission.
• First return-to-launch-site and catch attempt for a Super Heavy V3 booster.
• Super Heavy will execute launch, ascent, stage separation, boostback burn, and return to Starbase for a tower catch.
• Starship will deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites into orbit before attempting its first return to Starbase and tower catch.
• The 26 satellites will provide capacity equivalent to approximately 10 Falcon 9 launches carrying Starlink V2 Mini satellites.
• Satellites will deploy antennas and solar arrays, establish radio and laser communications, and raise their orbits using onboard thrusters.
• Satellites could begin serving customers within weeks of launch following successful on-orbit checkouts.
• Three Starlink V3 satellites will carry cameras to inspect Starship's heatshield and transmit imagery to ground operators.
• Starship's heatshield will feature improved tile retention, additional protection against plasma intrusion, and expanded use of curved tiles to reduce heating between tiles.
• Starship will only attempt its return and catch if critical reentry, landing burn, and tower approach systems are confirmed healthy.
• Multiple predetermined ocean deorbit locations and a passively safe suborbital trajectory provide contingency options.
• A successful mission would mark the first complete recovery of an orbital launch system, a major milestone toward rapid reusability.

posts.name: Elon Musk
posts.text:
SpaceX just released a detailed blog post explaining how Starship will return to Starbase for its first tower-catch attempt on Flight 15

and it is going to be the first full recovery of an orbital launch system

The mission brings together both sides of Starship’s future: delivering a major payload to orbit and bringing the entire launch system home for reuse.

Super Heavy will return minutes after liftoff, while Starship will deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites, fly a mission of more than 22 hours, then make its way back through the atmosphere toward the tower at Starbase, provided it passes the required vehicle-health checks

The update walks through the orbital safety checks, heatshield inspections, alternative splashdown locations, the precise approach over northern Mexico and southern Texas, and the final sequence of bellyflop, engine ignition, flip and catch

Flight 15 is targeting launch as early as Friday, November 13, pending regulatory approval. The 75-minute launch window opens at 4:45 p.m. CT. Here is the full plan, from liftoff to bringing both stages home

1. LAUNCH AND THE BOOSTER’S RETURN

Super Heavy will lift Starship from Starbase before the vehicles separate through hot-staging: Starship ignites its engines while still attached, then continues toward space as the booster turns back.

The booster will perform its boostback burn, descend toward Starbase and begin its landing burn roughly six minutes after liftoff. The catch is planned for approximately 6 minutes 35 seconds into flight.

This will be the first catch attempt for a V3 Super Heavy booster. SpaceX has already caught three V1 boosters, with two subsequently flown again.

2. THE HARDWARE DESIGNED FOR CATCHING

Super Heavy V3 has three grid fins instead of four. Each is 50% larger and significantly stronger, with a new catch point and revised positioning to support lifting and catching operations.

The tower’s mechanical arms......the chopsticks are shorter to allow faster movement and better tracking during a catch. Their main actuators have changed from hydraulic to electromechanical, improving speed, redundancy and reliability

These changes are part of the broader V3 architecture, designed around making recovery and reuse routine operations.

3. STARSHIP DOES NOT COMMIT TO ORBIT IMMEDIATELY

The ship initially follows a passively safe suborbital trajectory rather than entering a sustained orbit directly.

This is deliberate. If a problem occurs during ascent or shortly afterward, the trajectory takes Starship toward a cleared reentry area over the Indian Ocean without requiring a successful orbital mission.

After ascent, flight controllers assess the vehicle’s health and make a go/no-go decision for orbit.

With a go, one sea-level Raptor performs an orbital insertion burn approximately 26 minutes after liftoff, increasing Starship’s speed enough to establish orbit.

4. DEPLOYING 26 STARLINK V3 SATELLITES

Satellite deployment is planned to begin around 35 minutes into flight and finish around 1 hour 18 minutes.

Each Starlink V3 satellite adds approximately 1 terabit per second of network capacity. SpaceX compares this mission’s 26 satellites with roughly 10 Falcon 9 launches carrying V2 Mini satellites.

After deployment, the satellites unfold their antennas and solar arrays, establish radio and laser communications, and use onboard propulsion to raise their orbits. Customer service is expected to begin as soon as a few weeks after launch.

Three satellites have an additional job: photographing Starship’s heatshield.

Those images will be transmitted to operators and become one of several sources of information used to assess whether the ship is ready to return to Starbase. SpaceX has already tested this inspection method on previous flights.

5. ALMOST A DAY IN ORBIT

The planned mission lasts more than 22 hours, with approximately 14 orbits at an altitude of roughly 275 kilometers.

After deploying the satellites, Starship will coast for around another 21 hours until its orbit aligns with Starbase for the return.

Throughout that period, controllers will run continuous manual and automated checks. These cover engine health, power, communications, flight computers, navigation sensors, tank and feedline integrity, tank pressure and attitude control......the ability to maintain the ship’s intended orientation.

These checks are intentionally conservative. Returning to the tower is something the vehicle must qualify to do through its condition in flight.

6. ALTERNATIVE RETURN OPTIONS THROUGHOUT THE MISSION

The flight includes opportunities to end the mission early in precleared Pacific Ocean areas if the vehicle is not suitable for a Starbase return.

These include early- and late-mission splashdown options around Hawaii and a mid-mission opportunity several hundred kilometers off Chile’s coast. The same areas were used during Flight 14.

The mission therefore has multiple decision points rather than a single commitment to return home regardless of the vehicle’s condition.

7. THE DEORBIT BURN AND REENTRY

Starship will proceed toward Starbase only if it meets SpaceX’s internally developed, FAA-approved conditions for return and catch.

A single Raptor 3 engine will perform the deorbit burn, planned around 21 hours 36 minutes after launch. That changes the ship’s trajectory toward atmospheric entry over the Pacific Ocean, thousands of kilometers uprange from Starbase.

Reentry is planned to begin around 22 hours 11 minutes into flight.

The four control flaps will guide Starship along its intended trajectory while allowing small, deliberate turns to route it over sparsely populated areas of northern Mexico and southern Texas.

8. THE FLIGHT PATH BACK TO STARBASE

Starship will approach from the west and steer around the major cities of the Rio Grande Valley.

It will pass north of South Padre Island, continue out over the Gulf, then make its final turn south toward Starbase.

This is not an entirely untested maneuver: SpaceX has demonstrated the banking maneuver on previous Starship flights.

Residents of Cameron County and nearby areas may hear one or more sonic booms. What people experience will depend on weather and other conditions.

Reentry over land also has extensive spaceflight precedent, including the Space Shuttle, Dragon’s previous Florida returns, and Soyuz and Shenzhou missions.

9. HOW EARLIER FLIGHTS PREPARED THE HEATSHIELD

Previous ocean-return tests allowed SpaceX to deliberately push the heatshield, structure and control systems beyond the demands of a normal return to the launch site.

Experiments included removing dozens of heatshield tiles from critical locations and flying maneuvers that subjected the vehicle and flaps to higher heating and aerodynamic forces than a nominal reentry.

Flight 15 also retains Flight 14’s heatshield improvements, including additional tile-retention mechanisms in vulnerable areas, measures addressing plasma intrusion behind tiles, and curved tiles across a large portion of the shield to reduce heating between them.

The V3 rear-flap mechanism uses a single actuator with three motors per flap, improving redundancy while reducing mass and cost.

10. THE FINAL BELLYFLOP, FLIP AND CATCH

Arriving over Starbase, Starship will descend toward the tower at Pad 2 in its bellyflop orientation.

Shortly before reaching the tower, it will ignite its three sea-level Raptors, flip upright and stow its flaps.

Once vertical, it will reduce to two engines and maneuver between the tower’s arms. It will then reduce to one engine as it approaches a near hover.

The arms will close rapidly around two catch fittings just below the forward flaps.

Once Starship detects contact with the arms, it will shut down its final engine.

The ship catch is planned for approximately 22 hours 32 minutes after liftoff. All mission timings are approximate and subject to change.

11. SAFETY OPTIONS REMAIN AVAILABLE DURING REENTRY

SpaceX has built in options to end reentry before the ship reaches land if necessary, including intentionally tumbling the vehicle to ensure atmospheric breakup.

There is also a late option to divert into the Gulf if either the ship or the tower develops a problem that prevents a safe catch.

The objective is ambitious, but the return is governed by explicit vehicle-health requirements and multiple alternatives throughout the flight.

12. WHY THIS MISSION MATTERS

Catching the booster solves one part of the recovery challenge. Bringing the upper stage back from orbit addresses the other.

SpaceX described recovering the entire orbital launch system as the “Holy Grail of rocketry” the foundation for full and rapid reuse and an eventual airplane-like flight cadence.

That is the capability behind Starship’s larger mission: expanding Starlink, deploying the planned Starmind supercompute constellation, establishing a permanent human presence on the Moon and making life multiplanetary.

Flight 15 is taking SpaceX another major step toward that future: launch, deploy, orbit, return and bring both stages home

ref.text:
SpaceX’s Arizona data center, per a county supervisor: “We could be reducing property taxes across the board in Cochise County, the entire county, by 20%”

Frank Antenori, whose district includes the site, brought up the county’s tax math during a live Q&A:

“Here’s just something to just chew on. Arizona has an expenditure limit requirement that is placed on counties. If we exceed that expenditure, we have to rebate back to the taxpayers a certain amount.”

“So, if we’re receiving revenue in from SpaceX, by law, we have to offset that to the taxpayers. We have the potential to reduce, based on the projected revenue they’re creating, as much as 20%.”

“Let me just say it again. We could be reducing property taxes across the board in Cochise County, the entire county, by 20% to offset for the revenue here, because we can’t spend all that money. So, we have to give that money back to the taxpayers. The law says we have to.”

“So, you could see a potential significant impact to local property taxes. What that is, I don’t know. We’re going to have to do the math on it. But the law, if we have this large increase in property tax revenue, we have to balance those rates. So that will reduce dramatically the property tax burden of every resident in the county.”

“The construction sales tax, which also is the TPT, the transaction privilege tax, the retail tax, and the jail excise tax. So that will be part of the construction tax. We could literally use that money to pay the jail off in 2 to 3 years, as opposed to the 13 to 20 years.”

“So this could be a revenue to eliminate the half-cent sales tax in 2 to 3 years. We can get rid of that half-cent sales tax.”

But bringing a massive spacecraft back to the actual launch tower requires an entirely different level of confidence

SpaceX has been working to ensure the ship is reliable enough to return without damaging the tower or putting people at risk from falling debris

And SpaceX reached that point

Ship 42 is being prepared for the first attempt to catch a Starship upper stage with the launch tower

And there's another interesting detail

Elon highlighted that 42 is a special number, making Ship 42 a fitting vehicle for this historic attempt

This is the breakthrough Starship needs to achieve FULL AND RAPID REUSABILITY

For the first time ever, SpaceX is preparing to bring the entire Starship rocket back for recovery using its launch tower
